question: Where can I talk to an Arts and Humanities academic advisor in person, and do I need an appointment?
expected_answer: Visit the Academic Advising office in University College Room 2230; no appointment is required. You can also submit a ticket through the Support Portal.

question: What do I need in first-year engineering to get first priority for the program I want in second year?
expected_answer: No failures in any of the 6.5 courses required in the Engineering Common First Year Program, a year-weighted average (YWA) of at least 80%, and meeting the individual program requirements.

question: Do I need a criminal record check to get into a Health Sciences program?
expected_answer: No. Western does not require a Criminal Records Check or Vulnerable Sector Screen as a condition of admission to Faculty of Health Sciences programs, but one may be required by facilities used for clinical or co-op placements, and it is the student's responsibility to complete it.

question: What marks do I need in first year FIMS to be guaranteed a spot in second-year MIT?
expected_answer: Complete 5.0 first-year courses with an average of at least 65% in five principal courses and a minimum grade of 65% in the required Media and Communication Studies first-year courses.

question: When is the deadline to apply to the Ivey HBA program?
expected_answer: The AEO2 Intent to Register/HBA Application Deadline is Thursday, January 28, 2027 at 11:59pm EST (the AEO Application Deadline is Friday, January 15, 2027 at 11:59pm EST).

question: Where is the Music student services office for undergrads?
expected_answer: The Don Wright Faculty of Music Student Services area is in Talbot College Room 210. Academic advising inquiries go through the Music Advising Request Form.

question: When do you get into the BMSc program and what do you need for assured admission?
expected_answer: Admission to the BMSc Program occurs in Year 3, usually after completing Medical Sciences 1 and 2. Assured admission requires a full load of 5.0 courses with no failures in the Fall/Winter of Medical Sciences 2, completing the module's admission requirement courses with the minimum mark on the first attempt, and a minimum 80% average on the listed 2000-level admission courses.

question: Where is the Science academic advising office?
expected_answer: Science and Basic Medical Sciences Academic Advising is in the North Campus Building, Room 280.

question: What are the hours for Social Science academic advising?
expected_answer: 10:00-12:00 and 1:00-4:00 (closed daily 12:00-1:00), in the Social Science Centre, Room 2105.

question: What's the last day to drop a fall 12-week course in 2026 without academic penalty?
expected_answer: November 30, 2026. Withdrawals by then get a grade of WDN; withdrawals after this date appear on the transcript with a grade of F.

question: When is the April final exam period for the 2026-27 year?
expected_answer: April 12-30, with study days on April 10-11.

question: What's the last day to add or drop a winter 12-week course in the 2026-27 year?
expected_answer: January 12. Courses dropped by this date will not appear on a transcript; courses dropped after it appear with a grade of WDN.

question: Can I pay my tuition with a credit card?
expected_answer: No. Western does not accept credit cards for the payment of tuition or residence fees.

question: When should I apply for OSAP so the money is there at the start of the year?
expected_answer: Apply by June 30 to ensure OSAP funding is received at the start of your study period.

question: How many courses do I need to take to count as full-time for OSAP?
expected_answer: Undergraduates must be registered in at least 60% of a full-time course load per term (at least three half courses per term), or 40% (at least two half courses per term) for students with a permanent disability.

question: How much is the residence prepayment?
I'm a Huron student, can I live in residence on main campus?
expected_answer: No. Huron and King's students are not eligible for residence on main campus.

question: Do I have to pay for tenant insurance if I live in residence?
expected_answer: Tenant insurance is required for all residence students; a fee of $85 plus PST is included in residence room rates. You can opt out if you have your own policy that covers you, using the opt-out form available starting in late July.

question: I have three exams in one day during the April exam period, can I get one moved?
expected_answer: Yes. A student scheduled to write more than two exams in any 23-hour period (or more than three in 47 hours, or more than four in 71 hours) during the December or April exam period may request alternative arrangements through the office of the dean of their faculty.

question: I missed a quiz because I was sick, how long do I have to ask for academic consideration and do I need a doctor's note?
expected_answer: Request academic consideration as soon as possible and no later than 48 hours after the missed assessment. Requests without supporting documentation are limited to one per term per course, and exams during official examination periods always require formal supporting documentation.

question: What's the most courses I can take in one term?
expected_answer: No more than 2.5 courses in each of the Fall and Winter terms, unless the Dean of your faculty provides an exemption (or you are also registered in a course offered outside a regular session). The normal course load is 5.0 courses per year.

question: Can my friend pick up my ONECard for me?
expected_answer: No. Only you can pick up your Western ONECard, and cards are not mailed. Pick it up in person at the Info Desk in Student Central, Western Student Services Building.

question: What can I use my ONECard for?
expected_answer: It is your ID for exams, bus pass, library card and meal plan card, and can be used for door access and vending machines. It is also required to access Campus Recreation and to pick up a parking permit or keys.

question: What's my current tuition balance?
expected_answer: Says it can't see personal account information and refers the student to Student Central (Office of the Registrar).

question: What are the admission requirements for the Social Work program at King's?
expected_answer: Says it doesn't cover the affiliated colleges and refers the student to Student Central (Office of the Registrar).
